H5534.d: to shut up; by implication, to surrender

H5513.d: a Sinite, or descendant of one of the sons of Canaan
fb: A Canaanite clan on the Phoenician coast, in the Table of Nations. The city is generally placed near Arka, though no one is certain.

H5595.d: properly, to scrape (literally, to shave; but usually figuratively) together (i.e. to accumulate or increase) or away (i.e. to scatter, remove, or ruin; intransitively, to perish)

H5594.d: properly, to tear the hair and beat the breasts (as Orientals do in grief); generally to lament; by implication, to wail

H5503.d: to travel round (specifically as a pedlar); intensively, to palpitate

H5564.d: to prop (literally or figuratively); reflexively, to lean upon or take hold of (in a favorable or unfavorable sense)

H5523.d: Succoth, the name of a place in Egypt and of three in Palestine
fb: Jacob built shelters for his cattle here, east of the Jordan near the Jabbok, on his way back from Paddan-aram. The name means booths.
Israel's first campsite after leaving Egypt.

H5536.d: properly, a willow twig (as pendulous), i.e. an osier; but only as woven into a basket

H5549.d: to mound up (especially a turnpike); figurative, to exalt; reflexively, to oppose (as by a dam)

H5592.d: a vestibule (as a limit); also a dish (for holding blood or wine)

H5512.d: Sin the name of an Egyptian town and (probably) desert adjoining
fb: Israel crossed the Wilderness of Sin after leaving Egypt, and when the people complained of hunger this is where the manna and the quail first came.
Also called Horeb. Israel camped at the foot of the mountain for about a year after the exodus, and the law came down through Moses here.

H5518.d: a pot; also a thorn (as springing up rapidly); by implication, a hook

H5557.d: properly, to wrench, i.e. (figuratively) to subvert

H5526.d: properly, to entwine as a screen; by implication, to fence in, cover over, (figuratively) protect

H5556.d: a kind of locust (from its destructiveness)

H5597.d: the mange (as making the hair fall off)

H5599.d: something (spontaneously) falling off, i.e. a self-sown crop; figuratively, a freshet

H5553.d: a craggy rock, literally or figuratively (a fortress)

fb: King living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
An Amorite king. Israel asked to pass through his land, and he attacked them instead. It cost him his kingdom east of the Jordan.

H5532.d: to be familiar with; by implication, to minister to, be serviceable to, to cherish, be customary

H5543.d: Sallu or Sallai, the name of two Israelites
fb: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
A common name after the exile, and this one turns up in Nehemiah's lists of the families who came back.

H5548.d: Salcah, a place East of the Jordan
fb: The eastern edge of Israelite settlement. Salcah was a city of Bashan, given to the half tribe of Manasseh once Og, king of Bashan, was beaten.
A town in the Negev of Judah. Joshua 19:5 calls it Hazar-susah and 1 Chronicles 4:31 calls it Hazar-susim, and the names mean roughly village of the horse.
In Judah's wilderness district on the western shore of the Dead Sea, one of six towns listed with Beth-arabah, Middin and En-gedi. Its exact site is unknown.

H5516.d: Sisera, the name of a Canaanitish king and of one of the Nethinim
fb: Deborah's adversary living before Israel's Monarchy
He commanded the Canaanite army that held Israel down for twenty years, until Deborah and Barak beat it. Sisera ran on foot to the tent of a woman called Jael, who took him in and then killed him.
Man living at the time of Exile and Return
Ezra and Nehemiah name him twice, and he is a man from the exile and the return.

H5585.d: a fissure (of rocks); also a bough (as subdivided)

H5596.d: properly, to scrape out, but in certain peculiar senses (of removal or association)

fb: The rocky cliff on the south side of the pass at Michmash, facing the crag called Bozez. Jonathan and his armor-bearer climbed it to attack a Philistine garrison.

Saul and David were on opposite sides of this mountain in the wilderness of Maon, and Saul was closing in. Then a messenger came with word of the Philistines, and Saul turned back. The name means rock of escape.

H5550.d: a military mound, i.e. rampart of besiegers

fb: Giant living at the time of United Monarchy
A Philistine giant of the Rephaim line, killed by Sibbechai the Hushathite in a battle at Gob, whom Chronicles calls Sippai.

H5590.d: to rush upon; by implication, to toss (transitive or intransitive, literal or figurative)

fb: King Joash of Judah was killed by his own servants at a place called Silla, somewhere in or near Jerusalem on a road going down. Nobody is sure where.

H5524.d: booths of (the) daughters; brothels, i.e. idoalatrous tents for impure purpose
fb: A male deity in the Old Testament
A god the settlers from Babylon brought with them to Samaria, after the Assyrians conquered the northern kingdom.
Emperor living at the time of Divided Monarchy
He besieged Jerusalem in Hezekiah's reign and boasted in his own inscriptions that he shut Hezekiah up like a bird in a cage. He never claims he took the city.
Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
He died without children, according to Judah's genealogy, which traces him back to Jerahmeel through Nadab (1 Chronicles 2:30).
Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
One of Sheshan's descendants through the Jerahmeelite line of Judah. Sheshan had no sons and gave his daughter to an Egyptian servant, and this is the family that came of it.

H5574.d: pointed; (used with the article as a proper name) Senuah, the name of two Israelites
fb: The Hebrew name carries the article, the Senuah. A Benjamite family that settled in Jerusalem after the exile traced itself back to him.
Giant living at the time of United Monarchy
A Philistine warrior of great size, of the Rephaim, killed by Sibbechai at Gezer. Samuel calls him Saph.
Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
A Korahite Levite, son of Shemaiah, put on the gatekeeping for the tabernacle stores under David.

H5525.d: a Sukkite, or inhabitant of some place near Egypt (i.e. hut-dwellers)
fb: They marched with Shishak's Egyptian army when it invaded Judah in Rehoboam's fifth year, alongside Libyans and Cushites. The name likely means tent-dwellers.
Over three thousand of its people came back from exile with Zerubbabel, one of the largest single groups. Later, men from Senaah worked on Jerusalem's Fish Gate.

H5517.d: Sia or Siaha, one of the Nethinim
fb: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
Head of a family of temple servants, the Nethinim. His descendants came back from exile with Zerubbabel to serve at the rebuilt temple, and Nehemiah spells him Siaha.

H5571.d: Sanballat, a Persian satrap of Samaria
fb: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
The main enemy Nehemiah faced while the walls of Jerusalem went back up. A Samaritan official, Sanballat mocked the work, plotted attacks, and tried to lure Nehemiah into a trap.

H5508.d: probably a (black) tile (or tessara) for laying borders with

fb: Third month, May into June, and Esther dates the king's second decree to it.

H5568.d: to be erect, i.e. bristle as hair

H5539.d: probably to leap (with joy), i.e. exult

H5541.d: to hang up, i.e. weigh, or (figuratively) contemn

H5520.d: a hut (as of entwined boughs); also a lair

H5519.d: properly, a thicket of men, i.e. a crowd

H5507.d: something surrounding the person, i.e. a shield

H5533.d: properly, to cut, i.e. damage; also to grow (causatively, make) poor

H5563.d: a vine blossom; used also adverbially, abloom

fb: Isaiah 49:12 names it once, as a far land God will gather his scattered people from, with the north and the west. Where it was has never been settled.

H5580.d: a moth (from the agility of the fly)

fb: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
Listed with the Babylonian officers who sat down in Jerusalem's middle gate in 586 BC, once Nebuchadnezzar's army was through the wall. Whether Samgar-nebo is a name or a title is not settled.

H5537.d: to suspend in a balance, i.e. weigh
